amendments.title: From the tap on, the engine refuses new writes; what was already in hand is counted and kept for that person
amendments.rule:
Founder answer A decides this: nothing queued is thrown away at sign-out, so the window the probe found is closed in the ENGINE, in three parts, and the leave flow's order stays exactly as it is (end → sweep → forgetDrafts → signOut).

(m1) THE GATE. `end()` sets `ended` synchronously on entry (it already does, engine.ts:320). From that instant every public write — `enqueue` (:794), `recordGpsPoint` (:1185), `retry` (:1052), `discard` (:1074) — checks `this.ended` synchronously at entry, BEFORE its first `await`, and rejects with `SyncEngineEndedError` (exported from engine.ts and shared.ts: `name = 'SyncEngineEndedError'`, `code = 'ended'`, message 'This phone is signing out; nothing more can be saved on it. Sign in again and enter it once more.'). The same error after `end()` has finished: `requireStore()` (:1241) throws the ended error whenever `ended` is true and keeps its old sentence otherwise. `flush()`/`sync()` already no-op on `!started`/`ended` and are unchanged. A refused write is never written, so it can never be deleted.

(m2) WRITES IN HAND. A write that passed the gate registers itself in `this.writes: Set<Promise<void>>` from before its first `await` until after its bus emit (a `finally` deletes it). `settled()` (:340) awaits `opening`, then loops over `flushChain`, `syncing` AND every promise in `writes`, and returns only when one pass finds all three unchanged and `writes` empty — the same loop shape as today with the writes added. So a write that began a microtask before the tap lands whole before anything is dropped; `end()` never drops a table under an enqueue transaction.

(m3) THE RE-COUNT. After `settled()`, `end()` calls `refreshCounts()` again. If `keepQueue` is false and `pending + rejected > 0` now, `end()` proceeds EXACTLY as `keepQueue: true` (read set dropped, `_outbox` and `_sync_errors` and the file kept for that person, `userId`/`tenantId`/`deviceId` untouched) and reports it: `end()` returns `Promise<EndResult>`, `EndResult = { kept: boolean; pending: number; rejected: number }` (`kept` = the file survived, whether asked for or by the re-count). `LeaveSession.end` in react.tsx returns the same. The three apps' `LeaveSteps.end` (`Promise<void>`) accept it without change — return-type covariance — and `leaveNow` keeps its order: a kept file is still followed by the sweep of the OTHER files, `forgetDraftsOf` (a draft is not the queue) and `signOut()`. The GPS buffer still goes on every `end()` (amendment c); it is not in the re-count, and no app calls `recordGpsPoint` today (the delivery tracker keeps its own memory buffer, gps.ts) — the gate on it is API hygiene.

WHAT THE PERSON SEES. A write attempted after the tap: the screen's own error path, and never a 'saved on this phone' toast or navigation — sales orders/new.tsx:427-429 shows `place.error.message` (through `toApiError`, api-client errors.ts:175, today the generic 'Something could not be completed. Try again.' — see optional (q)); delivery deliver.tsx:416-418, collect.tsx:178-180, stop index.tsx:128-130 show the engine's own sentence; warehouse pick/[id].tsx:258-260 shows `start.error.message`. The sign-in screen follows when the session clears. A write that was in hand or completed between the tap's count and `end()`: it lands, is counted and kept; the screen had already shown it queued; that person's next sign-in on this phone sends it before the re-snapshot (exactly V5D). No sheet after the fact: the promise the sheet would make is the one the engine has just kept.

WHAT THE LEAVE FLOW SHOWS. Unchanged. The one-tap path shows no sheet and no overlay — the kit has no blocking overlay, and the account menu closes before `onSignOut` (native shell.tsx:329-330/465-466, web shell.tsx:417-418/680-681), so no UI state can be the guarantee and none is required to be. The sheet path keeps `loading={busy}` on its two buttons and swallows Cancel while a step runs. See optional (r) for the visible wait.

docs/27: §12 gains 'From the tap on the phone refuses new writes with a sentence; a write already in hand is finished, counted and kept for that person'; §13 test 13 gains the two cases below; §14 a row 'Sign out tapped while a write is in hand → finished, counted, file kept for that person; a write attempted after the tap → refused, never saved, never deleted'.

tests.name: DOS-167 a write that begins after end() has begun is refused and never deleted
tests.redBecause: The verifier's rig (a transport whose pull awaits a gate; engine started; pull held in flight; waiting() → {0,0}; `const ending = engine.end({ keepQueue: false })`). Then `enqueue`, `recordGpsPoint`, `retry('x')`, `discard('x')` must each reject with `{ name: 'SyncEngineEndedError', code: 'ended' }`, `status().pending` stays 0, release the gate, `ending` resolves `{ kept: false, pending: 0, rejected: 0 }`, `server.uploadCalls` is [], and after end() `enqueue` still rejects with the SAME name (not 'has not started yet'). Red today: enqueue resolves an opId and pending reads 1 (probe-race.json PROBE-A: refused null, pendingAfterEnqueue 1) and end() resolves undefined.

tests.name: DOS-167 a write in hand when end() begins is finished, counted and kept for that person
tests.redBecause: Case 1: a store wrapper over createMemoryStore() whose `transaction` awaits a gate; `const writing = engine.enqueue(op)` (passes the gate, blocks inside the transaction); sleep(0); `const ending = engine.end({ keepQueue: false })`; open the gate; `writing` resolves an opId; `ending` resolves `{ kept: true, pending: 1, rejected: 0 }`; `_outbox` still holds the op 'queued', `SELECT * FROM "retailers"` rejects no such table, readState 'userId' is still 'rahul', 'cursor' null; a restart as RAHUL with `recording()` answers manifest → upload → pull and uploads the same opId; a restart as AMIT on the same store uploads nothing and the outbox is empty. Case 2: `await engine.waiting()` → {0,0}, `await engine.enqueue(op)` completes, then `end({ keepQueue: false })` → `{ kept: true, pending: 1, rejected: 0 }` and the row survives. Red today: end() resolves undefined and the outbox table is gone ('no such table: _outbox', race2/probe.log).

amendments.title: The sheet's words: a 19-character keep button, the singular, and the truth about refusals
amendments.rule:
Meaning of answer A unchanged: queued changes stay on this phone for that person only and go the next time they sign in here; refused ones stay too but wait in Needs attention (the tray's name, docs/23 §8.11) and never go by themselves. Identical keys and strings in sales, delivery and warehouse strings.ts:

'leave.title': '{n} changes have not reached the office'
'leave.title.one': '1 change has not reached the office'
'leave.attention': '{n} need attention'
'leave.attention.one': '1 needs attention'
'leave.bodySignOut': 'They stay on this phone for {name} only and go the next time {name} signs in here. Nobody else can see them.'
'leave.bodySignOutRefused': 'They stay in Needs attention on this phone for {name} only. They do not go by themselves: {name} fixes or discards them there after signing in here. Nobody else can see them.'
'leave.bodySignOutBoth': 'They stay on this phone for {name} only. The queued ones go the next time {name} signs in here; the ones needing attention wait there for {name} to fix or discard. Nobody else can see them.'
'leave.bodySwitch': 'They go when you come back to {tenantName} on this phone.'
'leave.bodySwitchRefused': 'They wait in Needs attention until you come back to {tenantName} on this phone. They do not go by themselves.'
'leave.bodySwitchBoth': 'The queued ones go when you come back to {tenantName} on this phone; the ones needing attention wait there for you to fix or discard.'
'leave.sendNow': 'Send now'
'leave.signOutKeep': 'Sign out, keep here'   (19 characters; the founder's verb first, the body says what is kept and for whom)
'leave.switchAnyway': 'Switch anyway'
'leave.noSignal': 'No connection — they cannot go now.'

`leaveSentence` in each leave.ts: title = pending > 0 ? title(pending) : attention(rejected); the attention line = pending > 0 && rejected > 0 ? attention(rejected) : null; body = by (pending > 0, rejected > 0) → bodySignOut / bodySignOutRefused / bodySignOutBoth, and the Switch trio for a switch; a count of exactly 1 takes the `.one` key (the delivery app's existing convention, 'd1.loadSheets.one'). leave-sheet.tsx is unchanged (it reads labels through t()). docs/27 §12 quotes the new button name. Founder/UX may reword any sentence later; the three facts (count in the singular, refused ones do not go by themselves, every button ≤ 20 characters per libs/ui/src/types.ts:25) are the rule.

tests.name: DOS-167 the sheet counts one change in the singular, tells the truth about refusals, and keeps every button under the kit's 20 characters
tests.redBecause: {1,0,signOut} title must be '1 change has not reached the office'; {0,1,signOut} title '1 needs attention', body contains 'do not go by themselves' and not 'go the next time'; {0,2,switch} body contains 'do not go by themselves'; {2,1,signOut} attention line '1 needs attention' and body mentions both the queued and the ones needing attention; `catalogue['leave.sendNow' | 'leave.signOutKeep' | 'leave.switchAnyway'].length <= 20`. Red today: '1 changes have not reached the office', the refusals-only body says 'go the next time', 'Sign out, keep them here' is 24 characters, and the `.one` keys do not exist.

amendments.title: No read answers from the store until the identity is claimed
amendments.rule: Amendment (g) says nothing is rendered from any store before the identity is settled; engine.ts:222 sets `this.store` before `claimIdentity` (:233), so `outbox()` (:1141) and `needsAttention()` (:1151), which have no shapes gate, can answer from a foreign file for the length of the claim — and `useOutbox`/`useNeedsAttention` fire their first query the moment the provider sets the engine, while `start()` is still opening. In `start()`, keep the opened store in the local `store` and assign `this.store = store` only AFTER `claimIdentity(store)` returns (everything between already takes `store` as a parameter). `waiting()` is unaffected: it awaits `opening`, which resolves after the assignment. Defence in depth behind Layer A, two lines.

tests.name: DOS-167 outbox() and needsAttention() answer nothing until the identity is claimed
tests.redBecause: A memory store holding AMIT's queued op and a `_sync_errors` row (insert them with store.exec), wrapped so its FIRST `query` on `_sync_state` (claimIdentity's readState 'userId') awaits a gate; `const starting = rahul.start()` (identity RAHUL, fixedStoreFactory over the wrapper); sleep(0); `await rahul.outbox()` must be [] and `await rahul.needsAttention()` [] and `status().pending` 0; open the gate; `await starting`; both still [] because the foreign file was wiped. Red today: outbox() returns Amit's op during the claim because `this.store` is assigned at :222.

amendments.title: sweepIdentityStores closes a store it could not count
amendments.rule: In `sweepIdentityStores` (engine.ts:442-472) the catch at :467 only logs, so a store whose `createSystemTables` or COUNT threw stays open; on native expo-sqlite caches that connection and every later `deleteDatabaseAsync` of the same file fails 'currently open' for the life of the process. Wrap the count in try/catch per file: on failure `await store.close().catch(() => {})` BEFORE the log line, then continue to the next identity. The result shape `{ destroyed, kept }` is unchanged; an uncountable file is never deleted (the same rule tapLeave applies to the current file).

tests.name: DOS-167 sweepIdentityStores closes a store it could not count and never deletes it
tests.redBecause: A factory answering, for identity X, a store whose `query` throws 'database disk image is malformed' and whose `close` and `destroy` are counted; for identity Y a clean empty store. After the sweep: X's `close` called exactly once, X's `destroy` never, the log line 'sweep skipped a store' written, result `{ destroyed: 1, kept: [] }` (Y). Red today: X's close count is 0.

amendments.title: Optional: the refusal reaches the sales order screen in its own words
amendments.rule: `toApiError` (frontend/libs/api-client/src/errors.ts:175) maps a non-API error to kind 'unknown' with 'Something could not be completed. Try again.', so the sales order screen (orders/new.tsx:427-429) shows that generic line for a `SyncEngineEndedError` while the delivery and warehouse screens show the engine's sentence. Optional: a structural branch in `toApiError` — an error whose `name === 'SyncEngineEndedError'` (no import of @dos/offline; amendment h stands) → `new ApiError({ kind: 'auth', message: err.message, cause: err })` ('auth' is the kind whose meaning is 'sign in again'). Only wording; the guarantee in (m) does not depend on it.

tests.name: DOS-167 an engine that is signing out reaches the screen as a sign-in-again error in its own words
tests.redBecause: `toApiError(Object.assign(new Error('This phone is signing out; nothing more can be saved on it. Sign in again and enter it once more.'), { name: 'SyncEngineEndedError', code: 'ended' }))` must have kind 'auth' and that exact message. Red today: kind 'unknown', message 'Something could not be completed. Try again.'

amendments.title: Optional: a visible 'Signing out…' while a one-tap sign-out waits for a page in flight
amendments.rule: With a pull in flight `end()` can wait up to the request deadline (20 s) and the one-tap path shows nothing meanwhile; a second tap is swallowed by the running ref. Optional: in each Chrome render the kit's `Toast` with `open={busy && asking === null}`, message from a new string 'leave.signingOut': 'Signing out…' (2 words, within the toast's 6), `onDismiss` a no-op while busy. Not a guarantee of anything (the account menu closes before onSignOut), so not required; if added, the string goes to strings.ts of the three apps and the existing leave.test.ts catalogue check covers the key.

Pre-existing on main (`void switchDistributor(tenantId)`); not DOS-167's. Fix later: `run` catches and sets the sheet's `note`, or the switcher gets an error line.
S-row (from the design, restated) — the server-issued cursor carries no device identity: backend/libs/core/src/modules/sync/sync.service.ts:481-493; defence in depth only.

S-row (from the design, restated, P3) — identity files of people who never return are never swept; and the pre-DOS-167 unkeyed `dos.sales.draft.<retailerId>` keys are left at rest (frontend/sales-app/src/lib/draft.ts).
Not a row — the verifier's 'not proven on any platform' for store/expo-sqlite.ts destroy, the OPFS listing and the upgrade path: already the design's Step 8 platform proof.
notes:
Founder answer A decides the major without a new question: keep-for-that-person is applied to the window itself (a write in hand is finished, counted and kept), and the only thing the engine may still do after the tap is REFUSE with a sentence — never accept-then-delete. A refused write is not a loss (never saved, and told), so 'no order is ever lost' and docs/27 §14 'nothing is silently dropped' both hold. The three apps' leave.ts, leave-sheet.tsx and the layouts need no change for (m): `LeaveSteps.end` accepts the new `EndResult` return, and `leaveNow`'s order stands.

Rating: (m) is P0 — it is the P0's own loss path (it did not exist before DOS-167). Owner: the same lane, one fix commit over 3386a4e, libs test-first then the three apps' copy; re-verify, then my merge review.

Platform proof, two cases added to Step 8 (verifier, QA/tools/e2e): (1) cold-start sign-out — sign in as a rep holding a kept order, tap Sign out at once: the sheet reads '1 change has not reached the office' after the open and the file is not deleted; (2) the race on web — `page.route('**/sync/pull')` stalls one answer 5 s, tap Sign out, submit an order for Chavan Kirana inside the stall: the order screen shows an error line and never 'saved on this phone'; sign in again as the same rep: nothing waiting, and dos_qa holds no such order — or, if the write landed first, the strip shows '1 waiting' then 'Updated just now' and the order exists once.

For the main session's docs/22 rows the design's §8 sentence gains ', and from the tap on the phone refuses new writes while finishing and keeping any already in hand'. Merge note for lean-libs-offline-boot stands (DOS-046's `systemSchema` key must be placed in CLEARED_FOR_ANOTHER_IDENTITY or excluded like deviceId; docs/27 §4 paragraph re-read by the second to merge).
